newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Argentina offers 70,000 tonnes wheat to Manila.
newsitem.headline: Argentina offers 70,000 tonnes wheat to Manila.

text.p: Argentina has offered to supply 70,000 tonnes of wheat for the January 1997 requirement of Philippine flour millers, executives of local firms said on Tuesday.
"Argentina offered to supply soft wheat to us," an official in one of the country's largest flour millers told Reuters.
Soft wheat is used to make pastries and noodles.
Rumours in the market indicated two Philippine mills have bought 20,000 tonnes of Argentina wheat last Thursday. Philippine flour millers, however, said they are not aware of any transactions.
Traders said Argentina, Canada and Australia are positioning to get a slice of the Philippine wheat market.
The Philippines buys an average of two million tonnes of wheat a year, the bulk of them from the U.S. It is the fourth largest buyer of U.S. wheat, Manila traders said.
But rising wheat prices in the United States despite bumper harvests in other wheat producing countries forced millers to look for alternative sources.
On Monday, traders said two Philippine millers bought 35,000 tonnes of Canadian wheat at an average price of $178 per tonne FOB from the Port of Vancouver.
Manila traders said the prevailing price of U.S. spring wheat of $195 per tonne FOB from the Pacific northwest port was "unreasonable."
"It should come down some more to reflect bumper harvests in other wheat producing countries," an executive in a Manila firm said.
